hints: Focus on what type of compound calcium nitrate is and how Group 2 nitrates behave when heated strongly.
Remember the thermal decomposition of a nitrate gives an oxide plus two gases, one of which is famously brown.
Think about which of those two gases will affect a glowing splint, and how it makes the splint behave.
walkthrough:
**Recall the thermal decomposition pattern**

Nitrates of Group 2 metals (except ammonium nitrate) all decompose on heating in the same way. They form the metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.

$$2\text{Ca}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CaO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Describe the colour of the gas mixture**

Nitrogen dioxide, $\text{NO}_2$, is a very distinctive brown gas. Oxygen, $\text{O}_2$, is colourless. So the mixture seen in the test-tube looks brown because of the $\text{NO}_2$.

**Predict the glowing splint test**

A glowing splint relights in oxygen because oxygen supports combustion. Even though brown $\text{NO}_2$ is present, the $\text{O}_2$ also present will cause the glowing splint to relight. That matches brown gas plus relighting splint.

options.A: The gas colour is correct as brown due to $\text{NO}_2$, but the splint result is wrong. Oxygen is also evolved, and oxygen relights a glowing splint, it does not put it out.
options.B: This is correct. Brown $\text{NO}_2$ is evolved so the gas looks brown, and $\text{O}_2$ is also evolved so the glowing splint relights.
options.C: Both parts are wrong in logic. The gas cannot be colourless because brown $\text{NO}_2$ is always formed from nitrate decomposition, and the splint cannot go out because $\text{O}_2$ is present to relight it.
options.D: The splint result is correct because $\text{O}_2$ relights it, but the gas colour is wrong. Students choosing this may forget that $\text{NO}_2$ is brown, or confuse nitrate decomposition with carbonate decomposition which gives only colourless $\text{CO}_2$.
